heating_source.description: Choose a thermostat device or an individual device meter from Home Assistant Energy. Leave both blank to edit your current selections manually.

ev_source.description: Choose V2G Liberty or a Home Assistant device for entity suggestions. If your EV is listed as a battery in Energy, select that source here so LAHEMS2 only counts it as an EV. Continue without choosing a source to edit entities manually.

shadow_planning.title: Shadow planning forecasts
shadow_planning.description: Configure future quarter-hour data. Set the PV forecast under Solar and the accepted external schedule under EV when applicable.

data_description.demand_forecast: Use a sensor with future intervals in watts. Include heating loads and exclude EV power, solar and battery power.
data_description.import_tariff_forecast: Use a sensor with timestamped prices. When blank, LAHEMS2 checks the configured import price sensor for future intervals.
data_description.export_tariff_forecast: Use a sensor with timestamped prices. When blank, LAHEMS2 checks the configured export price sensor for future intervals.
data_description.planning_efficiency_percent: The same round-trip efficiency applies to all configured batteries in this comparison.
data_description.heat_pump_demand_forecast: Use timestamped power in watts already included in the household forecast. For pellet replacement, include only the heat pump load that serves spaces the stove can heat.

pellet_stove.title: Pellet stove
pellet_stove.description: Link the thermostats and temperature sensors in the rooms heated by the stove. The fuel estimate and heat-request switch are optional.

data.pellet_serves_forecast_load: Allow the stove to replace the configured heat pump forecast load
data.pellet_price_per_kg: Pellet price per kg (Home Assistant currency)
data.pellet_max_output_kw: Pellet stove heat output available to replace heat pump heat (kW)
data.heat_pump_cop: Assumed COP of the heat pump being replaced

data_description.pellet_stock: For a stove without a hopper sensor, use a Number helper in kg and update it when you check the hopper. Leave blank if stock is unknown. Percent estimates also require full hopper capacity.
data_description.pellet_serves_forecast_load: Enable only if the selected Heat pump electrical demand forecast describes zones the stove can actually heat.
data_description.pellet_price_per_kg: Divide the price paid by the weight in kg. For example, EUR 7.50 for a 15 kg bag is EUR 0.50/kg.
data_description.pellet_useful_heat_kwh_per_kg: Multiply the pellets' net calorific value (kWh/kg) by the stove efficiency. For example, 5.00 kWh/kg × 94% = 4.70 kWh/kg. If the fuel sheet uses MJ/kg, divide by 3.6 first. Count the same heat destinations here as in the output field below.
data_description.pellet_max_output_kw: Enter the stove's useful heat output available to the rooms or heating circuit in the selected forecast. Use the water-side rating if only heat to the circuit can replace the forecast load. Include direct room heat only where it replaces that load. Use thermal kW from the stove's specification.
data_description.heat_pump_cop: Enter thermal output divided by electrical input for the heat pump represented by the forecast. Match the outside and supply-water temperatures to typical heating conditions. For example, 8.2 kW of heat from 2.25 kW of electricity gives a COP of about 3.65.
